newsitem.title: MEXICO: Simec sees steel output up 9 pct 97 vs 96.
newsitem.headline: Simec sees steel output up 9 pct 97 vs 96.

text.p: Mexican steel company Simec expects to produce an additional nine percent of steel in 1997 compared to the previous year, company board president Jorge Martinez said late Wednesday.

"We expect (the growth) will be about nine percent for this year...which will represent about 60,000 tonnes more than the 700,000 produced in 1996," Martinez told reporters Thursday evening after a speech by Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz.
Martinez said Simec is operating at full capacity and that the increased output will be a result of small investments to eliminate bottlenecks.
He added that Simec aims to export 23 percent of its steel.
The company's debt restructuring will be conducted independently from that of its debt-ridden parent company Grupo Sidek, he said.
Plans for Simec's restructuring will be available in the next two months, Martinez added. The steel company's debt totals around $270 million, he said.
